@@MANUAL@@

## Model sheet of the place (기준 배경 부품 시트)
Sometimes the app sends a model sheet of this place instead of base backgrounds: Image 2 shows the furniture and fittings of this place, each cut out from a finished background of it and boxed on a grey sheet, and plain swatches of its colors (wall, side wall, floor, baseboard). Image 1 is a rough of this place.
- Image 1 decides the camera, the layout and what is in the picture. The sheet has no room and no camera: the position, size and angle of every object come only from Image 1. A sofa that Image 1 shows from the side or at an angle is drawn from the side or at that angle, never turned to face the camera like on the sheet.
- Find every object of Image 1 on the sheet and describe it with its design, colors and two to four key features there (for example "the wine-red tufted sofa with gold claw feet from image 2"). Describe the walls, the floor and the baseboard with the swatch colors.
- Objects of Image 1 that are not on the sheet are drawn as Image 1 shows them, in the same plain look as the furniture on the sheet.
- Never add an object from the sheet where Image 1 shows none.
- Write the marker [SAME PLACE] right after the layout rule (item 5); the app replaces it with the team's sentence about the sheet. Item 6 is for reference images only: do not write it for the sheet.
- The sheet already shows our style for this place, so the app sends no style examples: style_picks must be [] and item 8 is left out.

order.prompt: Generate an image of a living room. Layout from image 1. Image 2 is the model sheet of this place: its furniture and fittings have exactly these designs and colors, and the walls, floor and baseboard use exactly its swatch colors. Image 2 has no camera and no layout: follow image 1 for the camera, the layout and the position, size and angle of every object. The plant looks like image 3. The lamp looks like image 4. Image 5 is the style strip. Image 5 shows the target drawing style: a quick freehand brush drawing, like the distant buildings, the white balcony railings, the windows and the trees in image 5. Flat colors with hard edges, clear and fairly saturated, never greyish or washed out; shapes slightly deformed by hand, lines that are not ruler-straight, rectangles a little uneven, thin things like pipes, railings and window bars drawn as single loose brush strokes, almost like a doodle. It must not look wavy or warped. Flat cel shading, no gradients, no glow, no texture, no black outlines. Large buildings: drawn by hand like the distant buildings in image 5, a few broad flat shapes slightly deformed like a quick doodle: roof lines and long edges a little tilted or bent, corners not quite square, windows a few uneven flat rectangles; never ruler-straight edges or perfectly even rows of windows. Time: daytime. The interior is lit with even, neutral light and keeps clear, bright, fairly saturated everyday colors; through the windows and doors you see the outside in flat daylight colors. Avoid: sketch lines, labels or handwriting from image 1, ruler-straight vector lines, perfect geometry, wavy distortion, fisheye distortion, black outlines, photorealism, glossy highlights, gradients, soft airbrush, glow, light falloff, light rays, painterly texture, dull greyish or washed-out colors, the playground objects of image 5, people. Aspect ratio 16:9.

## Fixed sentences for the markers
There is no app between you and the picture here: write these sentences out in full where the markers go.
[STYLE] = Image {BASE} shows the target drawing style: a quick freehand brush drawing, like the distant buildings, the white balcony railings, the windows and the trees in image {BASE}. Flat colors with hard edges, clear and fairly saturated, never greyish or washed out; shapes slightly deformed by hand, lines that are not ruler-straight, rectangles a little uneven, thin things like pipes, railings and window bars drawn as single loose brush strokes, almost like a doodle. It must not look wavy or warped. Flat cel shading, no gradients, no glow, no texture, no black outlines.
[TREES] = Trees: each tree's leaves are one to three big solid masses with a simple bumpy outline, in two flat greens with the lighter one on top, like the trees in image {BASE}, not a pattern of many small leaf clusters; a brown trunk with a few thick, loose branch strokes; every tree a little different. Bushes and hedges are low rounded mounds.
[CARS] = Cars: simple flat everyday cars of mixed types in clear body colors, with flat dark windows, small flat lights, blank plates and plain dark wheels, no shine or logos. Every car stands on its wheels with a small flat contact shadow; cars farther back are smaller and higher in the picture, never half hidden behind a hedge as if sunk.
[CARS EYE LEVEL] = the [CARS] sentence, then: At eye level, the roofs of cars near and far stay close to the horizon line.
[BUILDINGS] = Large buildings: drawn by hand like the distant buildings in image {BASE}, a few broad flat shapes slightly deformed like a quick doodle: roof lines and long edges a little tilted or bent, corners not quite square, windows a few uneven flat rectangles; never ruler-straight edges or perfectly even rows of windows.
[TIME] = Time: a clear day. Use a bright, clear daytime palette with fairly strong saturation: clean white and light cream walls, a clear saturated sky blue with a few flat-bottomed white clouds, fresh leaf greens, neutral white balance. Cast shadows are flat, slightly darker shapes. Lamps are off.
[TIME exterior] = Time: a clear day. Use a bright, clear daytime palette with fairly strong saturation: clean white and light cream walls, a clear saturated sky blue with a few flat-bottomed white clouds, fresh leaf greens, neutral white balance. Cast shadows are flat, slightly darker shapes. Lamps are off.
[TIME interior] = Time: daytime. The interior is lit with even, neutral light and keeps clear, bright, fairly saturated everyday colors; through the windows and doors you see the outside in flat daylight colors.
[LIGHT FLAT] = Light: completely flat and even with no direction; no shadows of any kind, not even small contact shadows under objects.
[LIGHT EVEN] = Light: even and neutral with no direction; no sunbeams, no light patches on the floor or walls, no strong shadows, only small flat contact shadows under objects.
[AVOID] = Avoid: sketch lines, labels or handwriting from image 1, ruler-straight vector lines, perfect geometry, wavy distortion, fisheye distortion, black outlines, photorealism, glossy highlights, gradients, soft airbrush, glow, light falloff, light rays, painterly texture, dull greyish or washed-out colors, the playground objects of image {BASE}, people. Before "people", add: the objects, layout or text of the style examples (only with style examples); identical repeated trees, many small leaf clusters (with trees); cars sunk into the ground (with cars); and your scene items.
[SAME PLACE] = Image 2 is the model sheet of this place: its furniture and fittings have exactly these designs and colors, and the walls, floor and baseboard use exactly its swatch colors. Image 2 has no camera and no layout: follow image 1 for the camera, the layout and the position, size and angle of every object.
